title: Vesper and the Signal
premise: Theo Lockridge has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's derelict seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a fleet that stopped listening. When the ship Vesper returns from a forty-year deep-space survey with its crew mysteriously aged backward into children, Theo becomes the only adult witness to what they found: proof that the fleet's ruling council engineered the colony's abandonment. As the children's memories return in fragments and the council's enforcers close in, Theo must smuggle them—and the evidence—across a frozen continent to the cryo-banks, where half of humanity sleeps under a truce set to expire. In the end, Theo sacrifices his own place in the waking world, choosing to stay behind and keep the signal alive so that both halves of humanity, waking together, remember what was done.
about_author: Rosalind Blackwood is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural records before turning to fiction full-time. She writes slow-burning science fiction about forgotten places and the people who refuse to leave them.

chapters.title: The Last Caretaker
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Establishes his solitary routine inside the seed vault: checking germination trays, logging frost damage, recording broadcasts no one answers. The emotional beat is quiet grief disguised as duty, ending when his long-range array picks up an impossible return ping from deep space.

chapters.title: A Ship Called Vesper
chapters.summary: POV Theo. He tracks the vessel's descent through aurora-lit skies and treks across the ice to the crash-landing site. Inside, he finds forty crew members biologically aged backward into children, alive but disoriented. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as he realizes he is now responsible for lives he cannot save alone.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: POV Theo, alternating with eight-year-old Mira Chen, the Vesper's former captain. The children don't remember their voyage; Mira only recalls a locked room and a voice telling her to forget. Beat: Theo's loneliness breaks against the chaos of caring for them, and something like family begins.

chapters.title: Signals Old and New
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Deciphering the Vesper's damaged logs, he finds encrypted transmissions between the ship and the fleet council—dated after the colony was declared lost. Someone knew Earth survived. Beat: the first crack in his loyalty; the fleet he still serves may have lied for decades.

chapters.title: The Council's Ear
chapters.summary: POV Mira. A council probe drone arrives, scanning the wreck. Mira, half-remembering her captaincy, instinctively hides the children while Theo feeds the drone false telemetry. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve—they are being watched by the people who were supposed to rescue them.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Among the vault's legacy data he discovers the original colony charter: the fleet abandoned Earth deliberately, declaring it a write-off to consolidate power aboard the flagship arks. Beat: betrayal lands personally—the 'slow death' he recorded was policy, not accident.

chapters.title: Mira Wakes Up
chapters.summary: POV Mira. Her memories surface fully during a fever: she ordered the Vesper home carrying proof of the council's crime, and the reversal process was punishment, not malfunction. Beat: guilt and fury entwined; she must trust a stranger she can barely remember being older than.

chapters.title: Enforcers on the Ice
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A council retrieval team lands, officially to 'recover survivors.' Theo recognizes the euphemism from old purge records. He fakes a quarantine outbreak to buy time. Beat: the caretaker becomes a saboteur, crossing a line he cannot uncross.

chapters.title: The Long White Road
chapters.summary: POV Theo and Mira, alternating. They flee south toward the cryo-banks with thirty-one children, sleds, and the evidence core. Storms, thin rations, a child's broken leg. Beat: endurance as love; Theo teaches the children the survival songs his own mentors taught him.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity Sleeping
chapters.summary: POV Mira. At a relay station she accesses the cryo-manifest: two hundred thousand sleepers, split between loyalists and dissidents the council froze to silence. The truce expires in nineteen days, when the council decides which half wakes. Beat: the stakes become concrete and unbearable.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Was a Doctor
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Seven-year-old Devi regains his surgical memory mid-crisis and saves the injured child, then weeps without knowing why. Beat: tenderness and horror—the reversal stole their lives twice; Theo vows the waking will restore them, not just the powerful.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Relay Nine
chapters.summary: POV Mira. One of the older children, restored enough to remember his council ties, transmits their position before Mira can stop him. The enforcers' ships lift off within the hour. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh—a child torn between two versions of himself.

chapters.title: Running the Glacier Field
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A brutal chase across crevassed ice; Theo collapses a snow bridge to halt the pursuit, nearly losing Mira in the fall. Beat: desperation forging trust; she pulls him back from the edge, literally and otherwise.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Bank
chapters.summary: POV Theo. They reach the cryo-complex and find its hidden sublevel: the founders' original archive, including a lawful succession protocol the council buried. Beat: hope with teeth—there is a legal path to justice, if anyone survives to invoke it.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Become Three
chapters.summary: POV Mira. The council accelerates the truce deadline, broadcasting that 'recovered assets' justify immediate selective awakening. Mira decodes the succession protocol's requirements: a living witness, physical evidence, and a quorum of awakened citizens. Beat: the clock compresses everything.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Sleeping
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The children vote—truly vote—on whether to risk waking the dissident bank early, knowing it may kill some sleepers. Theo must let children decide an adult question. Beat: justice outside the law begins here, in a cold room full of small voices saying yes.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: POV Theo and Mira. The revival sequence runs; dissidents stir, some survive, some don't. Among the wakers is Elder Sefa Ibarra, the colony's exiled founder. Beat: grief and triumph braided together; the dead are named aloud before anything else happens.

chapters.title: Storming the Truce
chapters.summary: POV Mira. With Ibarra invoking the succession protocol, the awakened seize the cryo-control hub as council enforcers breach the perimeter. Theo holds the broadcast tower, transmitting the evidence fleet-wide. Beat: the climax—chaos, sacrifice, and truth going out on every channel.

chapters.title: The Cost of Staying Visible
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Wounded and cornered, Theo refuses evacuation, keeping the signal live until the council's own crews mutiny upon hearing the logs. The council faction falls. Beat: Theo's invisibility ends at the highest price—he is dying, and knows it.

chapters.title: Two Halves, One Morning
chapters.summary: POV Mira. She oversees the full, simultaneous awakening of both banks under the restored protocol, the children's reversed aging slowly undone by recovered medical tech. Beat: cautious joy; justice achieved without vengeance, per Ibarra's insistence.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Garden
chapters.summary: POV Mira. Theo, fading, is carried home to the seed vault. He plants the first open-air garden in forty years with the children around him, and records one final log—not a report, but a letter to whoever comes next. Beat: bittersweet peace; the signal continues past him.

chapters.title: Vesper Rising
chapters.summary: POV Mira, years later. Captain again, she leads the repaired Vesper back to deep space—not to flee, but to bring the outer colonies home. The vault's signal now reaches every ship. Beat: resolution and forward motion; Earth remembers, and this time, so does everyone else.
